Phosphine-Catalyzed Asymmetric Tandem Isomerization/
Annulation of Allyl Amines with Allenoates: Enantioselective
Annulation of a Saturated C −N Bond
Leijie Zhou, Xue Zhang, Qijun Wang, Min Liu, Wei Wang, Yongjun Wu, Liezhong Chen, *
and Hongchao Guo *
Cite This: Org. Lett. 2021, 23, 9173 −9178 Read Online
ACCESS Metrics & More Article Recommendations *sı Supporting Information
ABSTRACT: Under catalysis by chiral phosphine, an asymmetric isomerization/annulation cascade reaction of allylamines with
allenoates was realized. A wide range of γ-substituted allenoates were tolerated to a ﬀord chiral pyrroline derivatives in high yields
with excellent enantioselectivities. In the reaction, isomerization of readily available N-allylamines to reactive aliphatic imines
through a 1,4-proton shift is a key step, which circumvents the isolation of highly unstable alkyl N-sulfonylimines.
E
nantiopure ﬁve-membered N-heterocycles occupy a
prominent place in synthetic chemistry, and they are
also one of the most common key motifs in numerous
bioactive molecules, medicines, and natural products.
1 Thus,
development of their synthetic methods is of high value. In the
past two decades, phosphine-catalyzed annulation reactions
have been proven to be a robust, versatile tool for construction
of various cyclic compounds through a cycloaddition mode of
zwitterionic intermediates and electrophiles, especially in
highly enantioselective ways.
2 As one of the most typical and
representative annulation modes in phosphine catalysis, the
(3+2) annulation of allenoates and aromatic imines has been
investigated thoroughly
3,4 since it was reported ﬁrst in 1997 by
Lu.5 A large number of elegant methods were established,
providing convenient synthetic routes to various pyrroline-
cored skeletons (left, Scheme 1 a).
3,4 However, due to the
isomeric nature and relative instability, aliphatic imines are
rarely involved in this enantioselective (3+2) annulation
reaction. The only breakthrough in the application of aliphatic
imines was made in 2012 by Lu (middle, Scheme 1 a).
6
Through utilizing the diphenylphosphinoyl (DPP) group as
the protecting group of imines and amino acid-based chiral
phosphines as the catalysts, both high yields and enantiose-
lectivities were achieved with a broad range of aryl and alkyl
imines. However, the potential of variation at position 5 of
pyrroline products had not been evaluated. It is well-known
that synthetic chemistry greatly depends on the strategy of
preinstallations and sequence couplings and creates the core
chiral skeleton, in which preinstallations need to be performed
in ﬂexible alkyl substituents. Thus, simultaneously enabling
alkyl variations at both positions 2 and 5 is highly valuable for
the application of this annulation mode in chemical synthesis
(right, Scheme 1 a).
N-Allylamines represent a class of signi ﬁcant raw materials
and key intermediates in medicinal chemistry and the
pharmaceutical industry. Their transformations and application
have attracted a great deal of attention.
7,8 To circumvent the
challenge in preparing unstable alkyl imines, capturing reactive
alkyl imines in situ from isomerization of allyl amines is an
attractive strategy, which enables some previously elusive
design. For instance, the Terada group reported a relay
catalysis for a tandem isomerization/carbon −carbon bond
formation sequence of allyl amines in 2008 ( Scheme 1b).
9 The
reaction depended on the generation of reactive imines from
readily available allyl amines in a one-pot reaction via
isomerization, which enabled the functionalization at the
previously saturated α position. This double bond migration/
isomerization strategy inspired us to examine whether this
isomerization can be realized in organocatalysis for some
challenging transformations. As part of our continuing study of
annulation reactions,

catalyzed asymmetric tandem isomerization/annulation of allyl
amines with allenoates, enabling enantioselective functionaliza-
tion of a saturated C −N bond ( Scheme 1 c).
11 As shown in
Scheme 1 c, generation of reactive alkyl imine and its
subsequent capture in situ circumvent the isolation of highly
unstable alkyl N-sulfonylimines and are key steps.
At the outset of our design, we chose the reaction between γ-
isopropyl-substituted allenoate 1a and γ-sulfonamido-substi-
tuted vinyl ester 2a as the model reaction. As displayed in
Table 1 , without the use of phosphine as the catalyst, no
reaction occurred (entry 1). In the presence of achiral
phosphine PPhMe
2, the reaction worked to give the
anticipated product in 65% yield (entry 2). Various chiral
phosphines such as amino acid-based bifunctional chiral
phosphines ( P1 and P2), SPINOL-based chiral phosphines
(P3 and P4), and chiral bisphosphine P5 were investigated, in
which only bifunctional chiral phosphine P2 showed a
relatively low catalytic activity with poor enantioselectivity
(entries 3 −7). To our delight, when we turned to the
commercially available bicyclic chiral phosphine P6,t h e
desired product 3aa was obtained in a moderate yield with
excellent enantioselectivity (entry 8). Inspired by this result,
we changed the solvent to toluene and reversed the 1a:2a
substrate ratio and thus optimized the result to 75% yield and
97% ee (entries 9 and 10). Further adjustment of the substrate
ratio caused a minor decrease in catalytic activity (entries 11
and 12). Other analogues ( P7−P9) of chiral phosphine P6 led
to signi ﬁcant decreases in yields and minor decreases in
enantioselectivities (entries 13 −15, respectively). Catalysts
P3−P9 all belong to the dialkyl arylphosphine group; however,
there are huge distinctions in the catalytic reactivities. The
reason might be their di ﬀerent three-dimensional structure.
With the optimized conditions in hand, γ-substituted
allenoates, which were easily prepared from various substituted
acetic acids (see the Supporting Information), were examined.
As displayed in Figure 1 , the results indicated that methyl or
branched alkyl substituents at the γ position of allenoate seem
to have a remarkably positive in ﬂuence on the reaction. For
example, the allenoate having isopropyl, methyl, or tert-butyl at
the γ position worked well in this reaction with high yield and
excellent enantioselectivity ( 3aa−3ac). However, allenoates
with linear alkyl substituents at the γ position exhibited much
less reactivity, while retaining the excellent enantioselectivity
(3ad and 3ae). The branched alkyl-substituted allenoates with
a stereogenic center smoothly a ﬀorded the corresponding
dihydropyrrole derivatives ( 3af−3ai) in moderate to good
yields with excellent enantioselectivities, despite poor diaster-
eoselectivities. Unfortunately, diphenyl- and triphenyl-substi-
tuted allenoates had no reactivity in this reaction, due to
unfavorable electronic properties ( 3aj and 3ak). Cyclo-
pentylmethyl-substituted allenoate can also a
ﬀord the desired
product ( 3al) with excellent enantioselectivities, albeit in
relatively low yields. In particular, cycloalkyl- and bridged
cycloalkyl-substituted allenoates exhibited both high reactivity

(65−87% yields) and superior enantioselectivity (95 −>99%
ee) to provide the corresponding dihydropyrrole products
(3am−3at), which further proved that the branched alkyl
substituents at the γ position of allenoates led to higher
reactivity. Bioactive molecule-derived allenoates were also
tested in this reaction. For example, the common drug
dehydrocholic acid-derived allenoate a ﬀorded the correspond-
ing product 3au in >99% de. In contrast, the drug
indomethacin-derived allenoate provided product 3av in 65%
yield and 79% ee. The other drug chlorambucil-derived
allenoate gave product 3aw in 99% ee. Unlike cycloalkyl-
substituted allenoates, aryl-substituted allenoate showed low
reactivity despite the superior enantioselectivity ( 3ax). In
addition, variations of the arylsulfonyl group of γ-sulfonamido-
substituted vinyl esters 2 may be tolerated, giving the
corresponding products 3ba and 3ca in satisfactory yields.
The absolute con ﬁgurations of products 3 were con ﬁrmed by
analogy to the results of single-crystal X-ray di ﬀraction analysis
of product 3ar (detailed in the Supporting Information ).
As demonstrated in Scheme 2 a, this phosphine-catalyzed
(3+2) annulation reaction is scalable, being able to accomplish
the synthesis of cycloadduct 3aa in 65% yield and 97% ee.
Scheme 2 b reveals that the product may perform diverse
transformations, while treatment of product 3aa with LiAlH
4
achieved reduction of the ester groups, a ﬀording diol derivative
4 in 72% yield and 98% ee. Further treatment of diol 4 with
triphosgene failed to a ﬀord an envisaged nine-membered ring
but generated dichloride derivative 5 in 88% yield and 92% ee.
Direct oxidation of product 4 by PCC produced dialdehyde 6
in 68% yield and 99% ee ( Scheme 2 b).
To further explore the reaction mechanism, some control
experiments were carried out ( Scheme 3 ). When the sulfonyl
protecting group of 1a was changed to Boc, the reaction did
not occur ( Scheme 3 a). Replacement of the ester group with
the benzoyl group led to no reactivity ( Scheme 3b). All of the
results veriﬁed that the unique properties of the sulfonyl group

and ester group have a crucial in ﬂuence on this annulation
reaction. A deuteration experiment was also performed to gain
further insights into the proton shift ( Scheme 3 c). Adding 3
equiv of D 2O to the model reaction mixture under optimized
reaction conditions led to the successful incorporation of
deuterium into the product, which indicated that an isomer-
ization of substrate 2a deﬁnitely occurred.
As shown in Scheme 4 , a plausible mechanism for this
tandem isomerization/annulation reaction was proposed on
the basis of results of control experiments and previous
studies.
2−4,11 First, phosphine P6 attacked allenoate 1a to form
zwitterionic intermediate Int-1. This zwitterion acted as a base
to deprotonate 4-sulfonamido-2-butenoate 2a to give inter-
mediates 2a-1 and Int-1′. 2a-1 performed a 1,4-proton shift to
aﬀord enamine anion 2a-2, which could obtain a proton from
Int-1′ to give imine 2a-3 with simultaneous regeneration of
intermediate Int-1. Intermediate Int-1 worked as a nucleo-
philic reagent for an attack on the C N bond of 2a-3 from
the re-face to generate Int-2, which then performed intra-
molecular addition to furnish annulation, producing inter-
mediate Int-3. A subsequent 1,2-proton shift followed by the
elimination of the catalyst led to product 3aa. The regenerated
catalyst continued to participate in the catalytic circle. The
results of DFT calculation demonstrated the rationality of the
proton shift in the catalytic process (see the Supporting
Information for details). It is worth noting that only α-addition
products were observed via this method. According to DFT
calculations performed by Dudding,
12 the regiochemical
outcome of the current reaction involved Lewis acid activation,
van der Waals interactions, and steric repulsion, and α addition
was favored in terms of energy, compared with γ addition.
In summary, we have developed an unprecedented tandem
isomerization/annulation sequence of allylamines and γ-
substituted allenoates through phosphine catalysis. This
reaction enabled the generation of reactive aliphatic imines
from readily available N-sulfonyl allylamine under phosphine
catalysis, thus realizing the challenging asymmetric (3+2)
annulation between aliphatic imines and γ-substituted
allenoates. A series of biologically important chiral pyrroline
derivatives were obtained in high yields and excellent
enantioselectivities. A wide scope of γ-substituted allenoates
prepared e ﬃciently from various substituted acetic acid
compounds were well tolerated under the mild reaction
conditions; in particular, those bioactive molecule-based
allenoates prepared from speci ﬁc drugs containing acetic acid
units also a ﬀorded good results. Further transformations of the
products showed their great potential in construction of
various bioactive enantiopure compounds. In addition, the
experimental results and DFT calculation demonstrated that
isomerization of allylamines to imines played a key role in the
reaction and the 1,4-proton shift was favorable. Further studies
of the usability of this reaction in the synthesis of heterocyclic
compounds for pesticide research are currently underway in
our laboratory and will be reported in due course.

Phosphine-Catalyzed Asymmetric Tandem Isomerization/
Annulation of Allyl Amines with Allenoates: Enantioselective
Annulation of a Saturated C −N Bond
Leijie Zhou, Xue Zhang, Qijun Wang, Min Liu, Wei Wang, Yongjun Wu, Liezhong Chen, *
and Hongchao Guo *
Cite This: Org. Lett. 2021, 23, 9173 −9178 Read Online
ACCESS Metrics & More Article Recommendations *sı Supporting Information
ABSTRACT: Under catalysis by chiral phosphine, an asymmetric isomerization/annulation cascade reaction of allylamines with
allenoates was realized. A wide range of γ-substituted allenoates were tolerated to a ﬀord chiral pyrroline derivatives in high yields
with excellent enantioselectivities. In the reaction, isomerization of readily available N-allylamines to reactive aliphatic imines
through a 1,4-proton shift is a key step, which circumvents the isolation of highly unstable alkyl N-sulfonylimines.
E
nantiopure ﬁve-membered N-heterocycles occupy a
prominent place in synthetic chemistry, and they are
also one of the most common key motifs in numerous
bioactive molecules, medicines, and natural products.
1 Thus,
development of their synthetic methods is of high value. In the
past two decades, phosphine-catalyzed annulation reactions
have been proven to be a robust, versatile tool for construction
of various cyclic compounds through a cycloaddition mode of
zwitterionic intermediates and electrophiles, especially in
highly enantioselective ways.
2 As one of the most typical and
representative annulation modes in phosphine catalysis, the
(3+2) annulation of allenoates and aromatic imines has been
investigated thoroughly
3,4 since it was reported ﬁrst in 1997 by
Lu.5 A large number of elegant methods were established,
providing convenient synthetic routes to various pyrroline-
cored skeletons (left, Scheme 1 a).
3,4 However, due to the
isomeric nature and relative instability, aliphatic imines are
rarely involved in this enantioselective (3+2) annulation
reaction. The only breakthrough in the application of aliphatic
imines was made in 2012 by Lu (middle, Scheme 1 a).
6
Through utilizing the diphenylphosphinoyl (DPP) group as
the protecting group of imines and amino acid-based chiral
phosphines as the catalysts, both high yields and enantiose-
lectivities were achieved with a broad range of aryl and alkyl
imines. However, the potential of variation at position 5 of
pyrroline products had not been evaluated. It is well-known
that synthetic chemistry greatly depends on the strategy of
preinstallations and sequence couplings and creates the core
chiral skeleton, in which preinstallations need to be performed
in ﬂexible alkyl substituents. Thus, simultaneously enabling
alkyl variations at both positions 2 and 5 is highly valuable for
the application of this annulation mode in chemical synthesis
(right, Scheme 1 a).
N-Allylamines represent a class of signi ﬁcant raw materials
and key intermediates in medicinal chemistry and the
pharmaceutical industry. Their transformations and application
have attracted a great deal of attention.
7,8 To circumvent the
challenge in preparing unstable alkyl imines, capturing reactive
alkyl imines in situ from isomerization of allyl amines is an
attractive strategy, which enables some previously elusive
design. For instance, the Terada group reported a relay
catalysis for a tandem isomerization/carbon −carbon bond
formation sequence of allyl amines in 2008 ( Scheme 1b).
9 The
reaction depended on the generation of reactive imines from
readily available allyl amines in a one-pot reaction via
isomerization, which enabled the functionalization at the
previously saturated α position. This double bond migration/
isomerization strategy inspired us to examine whether this
isomerization can be realized in organocatalysis for some
challenging transformations. As part of our continuing study of
annulation reactions,
10 we herein report chiral phosphine-

amines with allenoates, enabling enantioselective functionaliza-
tion of a saturated C −N bond ( Scheme 1 c).
11 As shown in
Scheme 1 c, generation of reactive alkyl imine and its
subsequent capture in situ circumvent the isolation of highly
unstable alkyl N-sulfonylimines and are key steps.
At the outset of our design, we chose the reaction between γ-
isopropyl-substituted allenoate 1a and γ-sulfonamido-substi-
tuted vinyl ester 2a as the model reaction. As displayed in
Table 1 , without the use of phosphine as the catalyst, no
reaction occurred (entry 1). In the presence of achiral
phosphine PPhMe
2, the reaction worked to give the
anticipated product in 65% yield (entry 2). Various chiral
phosphines such as amino acid-based bifunctional chiral
phosphines ( P1 and P2), SPINOL-based chiral phosphines
(P3 and P4), and chiral bisphosphine P5 were investigated, in
which only bifunctional chiral phosphine P2 showed a
relatively low catalytic activity with poor enantioselectivity
(entries 3 −7). To our delight, when we turned to the
commercially available bicyclic chiral phosphine P6,t h e
desired product 3aa was obtained in a moderate yield with
excellent enantioselectivity (entry 8). Inspired by this result,
we changed the solvent to toluene and reversed the 1a:2a
substrate ratio and thus optimized the result to 75% yield and
97% ee (entries 9 and 10). Further adjustment of the substrate
ratio caused a minor decrease in catalytic activity (entries 11
and 12). Other analogues ( P7−P9) of chiral phosphine P6 led
to signi ﬁcant decreases in yields and minor decreases in
enantioselectivities (entries 13 −15, respectively). Catalysts
P3−P9 all belong to the dialkyl arylphosphine group; however,
there are huge distinctions in the catalytic reactivities. The
reason might be their di ﬀerent three-dimensional structure.
With the optimized conditions in hand, γ-substituted
allenoates, which were easily prepared from various substituted
acetic acids (see the Supporting Information), were examined.
As displayed in Figure 1 , the results indicated that methyl or
branched alkyl substituents at the γ position of allenoate seem
to have a remarkably positive in ﬂuence on the reaction. For
example, the allenoate having isopropyl, methyl, or tert-butyl at
the γ position worked well in this reaction with high yield and
excellent enantioselectivity ( 3aa−3ac). However, allenoates
with linear alkyl substituents at the γ position exhibited much
less reactivity, while retaining the excellent enantioselectivity
(3ad and 3ae). The branched alkyl-substituted allenoates with
a stereogenic center smoothly a ﬀorded the corresponding
dihydropyrrole derivatives ( 3af−3ai) in moderate to good
yields with excellent enantioselectivities, despite poor diaster-
eoselectivities. Unfortunately, diphenyl- and triphenyl-substi-
tuted allenoates had no reactivity in this reaction, due to
unfavorable electronic properties ( 3aj and 3ak). Cyclo-
pentylmethyl-substituted allenoate can also a
ﬀord the desired
product ( 3al) with excellent enantioselectivities, albeit in
relatively low yields. In particular, cycloalkyl- and bridged
cycloalkyl-substituted allenoates exhibited both high reactivity

(3am−3at), which further proved that the branched alkyl
substituents at the γ position of allenoates led to higher
reactivity. Bioactive molecule-derived allenoates were also
tested in this reaction. For example, the common drug
dehydrocholic acid-derived allenoate a ﬀorded the correspond-
ing product 3au in >99% de. In contrast, the drug
indomethacin-derived allenoate provided product 3av in 65%
yield and 79% ee. The other drug chlorambucil-derived
allenoate gave product 3aw in 99% ee. Unlike cycloalkyl-
substituted allenoates, aryl-substituted allenoate showed low
reactivity despite the superior enantioselectivity ( 3ax). In
addition, variations of the arylsulfonyl group of γ-sulfonamido-
substituted vinyl esters 2 may be tolerated, giving the
corresponding products 3ba and 3ca in satisfactory yields.
The absolute con ﬁgurations of products 3 were con ﬁrmed by
analogy to the results of single-crystal X-ray di ﬀraction analysis
of product 3ar (detailed in the Supporting Information ).
As demonstrated in Scheme 2 a, this phosphine-catalyzed
(3+2) annulation reaction is scalable, being able to accomplish
the synthesis of cycloadduct 3aa in 65% yield and 97% ee.
Scheme 2 b reveals that the product may perform diverse
transformations, while treatment of product 3aa with LiAlH
4
achieved reduction of the ester groups, a ﬀording diol derivative
4 in 72% yield and 98% ee. Further treatment of diol 4 with
triphosgene failed to a ﬀord an envisaged nine-membered ring
but generated dichloride derivative 5 in 88% yield and 92% ee.
Direct oxidation of product 4 by PCC produced dialdehyde 6
in 68% yield and 99% ee ( Scheme 2 b).
To further explore the reaction mechanism, some control
experiments were carried out ( Scheme 3 ). When the sulfonyl
protecting group of 1a was changed to Boc, the reaction did
not occur ( Scheme 3 a). Replacement of the ester group with
the benzoyl group led to no reactivity ( Scheme 3b). All of the
results veriﬁed that the unique properties of the sulfonyl group

reaction. A deuteration experiment was also performed to gain
further insights into the proton shift ( Scheme 3 c). Adding 3
equiv of D 2O to the model reaction mixture under optimized
reaction conditions led to the successful incorporation of
deuterium into the product, which indicated that an isomer-
ization of substrate 2a deﬁnitely occurred.
As shown in Scheme 4 , a plausible mechanism for this
tandem isomerization/annulation reaction was proposed on
the basis of results of control experiments and previous
studies.
2−4,11 First, phosphine P6 attacked allenoate 1a to form
zwitterionic intermediate Int-1. This zwitterion acted as a base
to deprotonate 4-sulfonamido-2-butenoate 2a to give inter-
mediates 2a-1 and Int-1′. 2a-1 performed a 1,4-proton shift to
aﬀord enamine anion 2a-2, which could obtain a proton from
Int-1′ to give imine 2a-3 with simultaneous regeneration of
intermediate Int-1. Intermediate Int-1 worked as a nucleo-
philic reagent for an attack on the C N bond of 2a-3 from
the re-face to generate Int-2, which then performed intra-
molecular addition to furnish annulation, producing inter-
mediate Int-3. A subsequent 1,2-proton shift followed by the
elimination of the catalyst led to product 3aa. The regenerated
catalyst continued to participate in the catalytic circle. The
results of DFT calculation demonstrated the rationality of the
proton shift in the catalytic process (see the Supporting
Information for details). It is worth noting that only α-addition
products were observed via this method. According to DFT
calculations performed by Dudding,
12 the regiochemical
outcome of the current reaction involved Lewis acid activation,
van der Waals interactions, and steric repulsion, and α addition
was favored in terms of energy, compared with γ addition.
In summary, we have developed an unprecedented tandem
isomerization/annulation sequence of allylamines and γ-
substituted allenoates through phosphine catalysis. This
reaction enabled the generation of reactive aliphatic imines
from readily available N-sulfonyl allylamine under phosphine
catalysis, thus realizing the challenging asymmetric (3+2)
annulation between aliphatic imines and γ-substituted
allenoates. A series of biologically important chiral pyrroline
derivatives were obtained in high yields and excellent
enantioselectivities. A wide scope of γ-substituted allenoates
prepared e ﬃciently from various substituted acetic acid
compounds were well tolerated under the mild reaction
conditions; in particular, those bioactive molecule-based
allenoates prepared from speci ﬁc drugs containing acetic acid
units also a ﬀorded good results. Further transformations of the
products showed their great potential in construction of
various bioactive enantiopure compounds. In addition, the
experimental results and DFT calculation demonstrated that
isomerization of allylamines to imines played a key role in the
reaction and the 1,4-proton shift was favorable. Further studies
of the usability of this reaction in the synthesis of heterocyclic
compounds for pesticide research are currently underway in
our laboratory and will be reported in due course.
